Subject: Follow-up: parallel session priority matrix + next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before Ben and I put together a rate recommendation.

Recap (from Brightline requirements):
- Target 99th pct latency for streaming-first-chunk: <= 250ms.
- Sustained throughput target: ~700 QPS during peak (25% of traffic requires streaming responses).
- Concurrent active sessions: up to 120 parallel user sessions; peak fanout per session can be 2–3 simultaneous requests.
- Connection pooling: clients prefer long-lived connections from a small pool (target ~40–60 pooled connections per region).
- KV caching: reuse across sessions is expected for same user context.

Proposed clarifications / asks (can you confirm):
1) Is 120 the absolute max concurrent sessions (all regions combined) or per-region?
2) Do you expect peaks to be multi-hour (steady 700 QPS) or short spikes (minutes)?
3) Any regulatory constraints on retention or private deployment we should include in pricing?

Next steps from Redwood: Ben will draft a capacity-backed ratecard that includes: reserved concurrency bucket, burst capacity policy, and a suggested pooling strategy with connection and session priority tiers. I’ll attach an initial draft ratecard and a simple priority matrix for your review.

Deliverables timeline:
- Ben: draft rate proposal + pooling diagrams (48 business hrs)
- Aditya: technical note on streaming SLOs and fallback model variants (72 business hrs)

Attachments in this thread: redwood-ratecard-q4-v2.pdf (rate tiers), connpool-priority-matrix.xlsx (priority matrix), redwood-connpool-diagram.png (diagram).

If that looks right, I’ll mark these as action items and we’ll schedule a 30-min pricing review next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications: 

- The 120 concurrent sessions number is per-region (we’ll have a US primary and an EU DR region). Expect US to carry ~85% of traffic.
- Peaks are usually sustained for 1–2 hours during morning batch jobs and then short spikes (5–10m) during launches.
- Regs: EU data is subject to our DPA; we will likely require customer-managed KMS for EU workload.

On pooling: we prefer fewer long-lived connections from our edge fleet (so 40–60 per region sounds fine). Would Redwood recommend separate pools per priority class or shared pools with request tagging?

Procurement is particularly sensitive to committed concurrency vs burst billing. If you can show a clear cost for a 3x burst window, procurement can evaluate easily.

I’m looping in procurement (procurement@brightlinehealth.com) — they’ll want to see a line-item view and any proposed SLA for latency and availability. 

—Sarah

Thanks Sarah — helpful details. Attaching a short proposal and cost sketch. High level notes inline and a recommendation at the bottom.

--- Proposal summary ---
1) Concurrency model
   - Reserved concurrency (guaranteed): 120/session-bucket reserved for US region (matches ask).
   - Priority tiers: three logical tiers (Realtime, Standard, Background). Each tier uses token-based priority tagging; we advocate shared connection pools per region with token-based scheduling to simplify NAT and TLS state.
   - Expected connection pool: 50 long-lived connections per region (configurable).

2) Burst policy
   - Burst window: 3x reserved for sustained bursts up to 15 minutes without additional charge; beyond that, burst billing applies at a discounted overage rate. This aligns with your short spikes profile.

3) Streaming SLOs
   - First-chunk 99th pct: 200–300ms depending on model family; we can guarantee <=250ms for our medium-opt model under reserved concurrency.
   - Fallback: automatic downgrade to smaller model family if the primary variant exceeds latency SLO; failover is transparent to the caller.

4) Pricing sketch (line items)
   - Monthly reserved concurrency (120 units) — base monthly fee
   - Included burst (3x for up to 15 mins/day) — no charge
   - Additional QPS over sustained baseline — per-10k-tokens pricing slab
   - Dedicated connection pool instance (per region) — one-time setup + small monthly fee

5) Compliance / KMS
   - EU-focused deployment supports customer-managed KMS and dedicated VPC/control plane. Pricing delta for private deployment noted in attachment.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-q4-v2.pdf (detailed line items), connpool-priority-matrix.xlsx (priority matrix), redwood-connpool-diagram.png (pool topology).

Recommended next steps:
- Sarah/procurement: confirm that 120 reserved concurrency per region is acceptable and whether the 3x/15m burst envelope covers your peaks.
- If yes, we’ll convert this sketch into a formal quote + draft contract language (SLA latencies spelled out) and share a DocuSign pre-sign.

Forwarding the ratecard and pool diagram in case procurement needs a single packaged PDF.

--Ben
